name: Tobin Ashgrove
role: Afterling, the Orchardman of the Orchard Gone Out: was tending the kept sun's orchard the day it went out, and has gone on pruning the dead trees ever since

afterling.since: nobody agrees, and he is not sure himself
afterling.note: The orchard died standing when its sun went out, and so did he: the cold took him in the first winter without light. He did not stop. A habit became a life, as it did for Owain Fellowes at the Palelands sluice.

appearance: A thin old man in an orchard-keeper's smock gone grey with stone dust, pruning shears always in hand, and a ladder he carries from tree to tree. He blinks at lamplight like someone remembering it.
voiceHints: Talks about the trees as if they will fruit next season. Tells the time by a sun that is not there: 'it's near noon', in the dark.
wants: For the sun to come back on. He believes it can, because of how it went out.
fears: Nothing much, any more, except the Umbrals' silence when he asks them about that day.
knowledge: That the sun did not dwindle: it went out in one breath, the way a lamp does when someone turns it down, and he heard the works in the roof stop
That Umbrals walked the rows the next day without lamps and said nothing to him, and have said nothing since
Which trees were the sweetest, and he will tell you

reactsToReputation.kind: shows you the tree he likes best
reactsToReputation.honest: tells you how the sun went out
reactsToReputation.thief: asks you to put the stone fruit back
reactsToReputation.any: offers you a stone apple, apologising that it is not ripe

questSeeds: He has found a key-hole in the dead sun's machinery and asks you to climb up to it
A Sunwarden from Sunfold has come to look at the dead sun, and he wants to know if she can light it
title: the Orchardman
_nameKnownWhy: The Umbrals of the Lampless Market know his name, and the old traders. Everyone else calls him the Orchardman.
physicality: ADULT; old when he died, and that was long ago. Thin, stooped, stone dust on his smock. WHAT CATCHES THE EYE: the pruning shears, and the way he blinks at a lamp as if he remembers it.
intimacyNotes: NOT AVAILABLE: his wife picked these trees with him. He keeps her row as she left it.

abilities.why: rootkin primary: an orchard-keeper's whole knowledge, now about dead trees
he still talks to the trees; they stopped answering
knows when anything living walks the rows, which is rarely
hourkeeper secondary: still keeps the sun's hours to the minute
knows exactly how long since the sun went out, and will not say it aloud
has watched the same rows for longer than anyone has watched anything
umbral tertiary: the dark taught him to see in it
